newsitem.title: USA: Hungary to pay pensions for Holocaust victims.
newsitem.headline: Hungary to pay pensions for Holocaust victims.

text.p: Hungary, ending two years of negotiations, has handed over a check for $28 million which will be used to fund monthly pensions for up to 20,000 Hungarian Holocaust survivors, the World Jewish Congress said on Friday.

The WJC said Hungary's action move made it the first East European country to agree to pay such pensions, and that the money represented initial restitution for Jewish property that was confiscated by the Nazis and then nationalised by the Communists after the Second World War.
Similiar negotiations are being conducted with Poland and the Czech Republic, but the World Jewish Congress said negotiations with those two countries were not going well.
The negotiations are being conducted with the East European governments by the World Jewish Restitution Organisation, which is a branch of the WJC.
Under the terms of the agreement with Hungary, a foundation will be set up by the WJRO and the Hungarian Jewish community to administer the pension payments.
The WJC said it would report to the the U.S. Senate, which is considering Hungarian membership in NATO, that a satisfactory agreeement had been reached.
